findings.title: Vacuity controls sit inside the same test cell as the positive assertion, not in a separate MUTANT-titled cell
findings.evidence: S1-S4 each end with a `withRolledBackTx` block appended to the SAME `test(...)` callback as the positive read (e.g. lines 143-155 inside the S1 cell). The sibling batteries that also use `withRolledBackTx` (coa-template-pr-a.test.mjs, coa-template-pr-b.test.mjs) instead give a wall-breaking mutant its own dedicated cell, usually titled with "MUTANT" (e.g. `I-M1`, `§2.4b`, `§3.2 M6 MUTANT`), separate from the behavioural cell it backs.
findings.why: Not a WORK-ORDER violation (rule 4 only requires the new cell fail once against a broken subject and restore byte for byte, which this file does) and the file's own header states the convention up front, so a reader is not surprised. It is a real shape difference from the two other files that share this exact helper, and a grep for `MUTANT` finds nothing in this file, so a search that works on the siblings misses these controls here.
findings.fix: Optional: no change needed to pass review. If this shape becomes the template other wave-4 lanes copy, consider naming these blocks (a trailing `t.step` or a comment banner reading MUTANT/VACUITY) so a `grep MUTANT` sweep across `packages/db/tests` still finds every wall-breaking check.
